Beebeeb Desktop, first release. End-to-end encrypted, zero-knowledge cloud storage — a native sync client for Windows and Linux.

## What's new

Everything — this is the first build.

### Sync
- Sign in and unlock your zero-knowledge vault (password, optional 2FA, and 12-word recovery phrase support)
- On-demand file access on Windows via the Cloud Files API — files appear instantly as placeholders and download only when you open them
- Selective sync: choose exactly which folders sync to this device
- Known-folder backup: mirror Desktop/Documents/Pictures into your vault
- Conflict handling that never silently drops your work — concurrent edits become a renamed "Keep Both" copy, with full version history to restore any prior version
- Background sync engine with automatic retry and an offline queue

### App
- Runs in the system tray — pause/resume sync, view recent activity, no console window
- Optional launch at login
- Signed, automatic updates verified before install
- Diagnostics export, for when something needs a closer look

### Security
- Files are encrypted on your device before upload — Beebeeb never has your key
- Session credentials live in your OS keychain, not on disk in plaintext
- Warnings before opening risky file types (.exe, .bat, .ps1, and similar) synced from shared folders

## Platforms in this release

- **Windows** — MSI and NSIS installers, signed
- **Linux** — AppImage, .deb, .rpm
- **macOS** — not yet. The Finder integration needs a bit more engineering (universal build support) plus code-signing and notarization credentials. Tracked separately, coming in a future release.

## Known limitations

- Large files are hydrated in full on open rather than by range — works correctly, just not bandwidth-optimal yet for big files
- No thumbnail previews for images/video in Windows Explorer yet
- No dedicated uninstall/remount helper yet — standard OS uninstall works, just not a guided flow

## Roadmap

- macOS release (Finder integration, signed and notarized)
- Explorer thumbnail previews (images, video)
- Range-based partial file hydration for large files
- Guided uninstall/remount flow

If something looks broken, tell us — this is early software and we'd rather know.
